content.label: The real course, imported and read as a student
content.lead: I took the course file off your ticket, imported it here, published it, and opened its discussions the way a learner would.

before.caption: Before — a real discussion out of the course, arriving as one unbroken block of punctuation

after.caption: After — the same discussion as a banner, a titled section, headings, paragraphs and a bulleted list

blocks.text: All eleven discussions in that course were opened one by one, not just this one. Every one of them now reads as a page, and none of them shows a leftover symbol. Between them they cover every kind of formatting the course actually uses: banners and icons, two sizes of heading, dividing rules, bulleted and numbered lists.

The course is the one linked on the ticket — the public-HR course from the university export. It brings in thirteen sections and a hundred and twenty activities, eleven of them discussions, each carrying between a thousand and two thousand two hundred characters of formatting. It is sitting in the local workspace now, so you can open it yourself.

content.label: An icon that swamped its own heading
content.lead: Found on that first real import: the small icon a heading opens with came through at nine times its intended size, and landed above the words instead of beside them.

shots.caption: After the fix — the icon sits on the line with 'Insight Exchange', at the size the course author drew it

blocks.text: The course sets that icon to fifty pixels; the import drops the sizing, so it arrived at two hundred and thirty and pushed the heading text onto its own line. An image sharing a line with heading text is an icon, so it is now held to the height of that line. This is a patch on our side, in discussion descriptions only — the sizing is lost during the import itself, which is Artur's.

content.label: A stress case the real course does not reach
content.lead: The whole description arrived as one grey block of symbols; it now reads as a page.

before.caption: Before — headings, emphasis, a picture, a numbered list, a table and a quote all flattened into one paragraph of symbols

after.caption: After — the same words as headings, bold text, a picture and a numbered list

blocks.text: This one is hand-built to carry things the real course never uses — a table, a quotation, a link, code-styled words. It is here so those are not left untested.

content.label: Stray marks around inline code
content.lead: Found while walking through it with you: single words meant to look like code came out wrapped in stray marks.

shots.caption: After — the checklist at the foot of the description, with the code-styled words now clean

blocks.text: The marks were added by the styling, not by the author, so no amount of editing removed them. Fixed only for discussion descriptions. The same stray marks still appear everywhere else in the app that shows written content — it is not new and I have not touched it, but you should know it is there.

content.label: The author's read-only view
content.lead: The same screen an author gets when they can look but not edit.

before.caption: Before — symbols, exactly as the student saw them

after.caption: After — matches what the student now sees

content.label: The new preview, for authors
content.lead: The editing box still holds the source, because that is what gets saved — but there is now a way to see it as a student will.

before.caption: Before — the editing box only, no way to see the result without saving and opening the course

after.caption: After — a Write and Preview pair sits on the same line as the label. Write is unchanged

shots.caption: Preview — the same wording rendered exactly as the student will get it, without saving

blocks.text: Switching between the two changes nothing and saves nothing: the Save button stays greyed until you actually edit. The box keeps its height in both, so the panel does not jump. An empty description says there is nothing to preview yet. Available in all four languages.

content.label: Plain descriptions do change, in one way
content.lead: Where an author pressed return, a student now sees a line break. Before, those breaks were thrown away and the sentences ran together.

before.caption: Before — three typed lines run together into one flowing paragraph, in grey

after.caption: After — the same three lines, broken where the author broke them, in darker text

blocks.text: I first reported this pair as identical. They are not, and you caught it. The wording is untouched and nothing is lost, but the shape on screen is different: an author's line breaks are now honoured and the text sits darker. Every hand-written description that contains a line break will shift this way once this ships. You have accepted that — see the fifth decision below.

What the check was really for does hold. Characters that could have been swallowed by the new handling survive: that last line still reads 'Costs under ten dollars to join in' with the less-than sign and the ampersand intact, and no stray symbols appear.

content.label: Seeing a course as a student, step by step
content.lead: Nine clicks from the front door. Every one of them is pictured.

shots.caption: 1. Start on your workspaces list — the first screen after signing in
2. Click the workspace holding the course. You land on its dashboard
3. Click Learning Journeys in the narrow strip down the left. You get the list of courses
4. Click the course row. It opens on Outline, with four tabs across the top
5. Click the Publish tab. The course row now has a Preview as button on its right
6. Click Preview as. Two choices drop down: Instructor and Student
7. Click Student. A new tab opens on the course's first activity, signed in as a learner
8. In the left-hand course menu, click a lesson to open it up
9. Click the discussion. This is the screen the whole job was about

blocks.text: Two shorter ways in, once you know the long one. Inside any activity you are editing, the green Serving chip in the header lists the course's versions and each has an eye icon that previews that version as a student. Version insights, next to it, does the same. All three sign you in as a stand-in learner for about a day; the yellow Preview Mode strip across the top tells you it is in use.
That stand-in sign-in lives in the tab it opened. Copying the address into a fresh tab gives you a session-expired page rather than the course — go back through Preview as instead.

content.label: Two notes for Artur, whose import this is
content.lead: Both turned up while running his importer over the real course. Neither is mine to act on and neither is on our plan.

items: Pictures lose the size their author set. A fifty-pixel icon comes through at two hundred and thirty. I patched it for discussion descriptions; imported pages still show it.

The importer's own acceptance check disagrees with the importer on six of thirteen points — all of them about content he has deliberately started bringing in rather than dropping. It reads as a check nobody updated alongside two changes he has open today, not as a break.

blocks.text: The check never says anything on our machines or on the build server, because it quietly skips itself when the course file is missing, which it always was until today. The file now sits beside the code, so it runs.

decisions.title: Headings inside a description are capped so they never outrank the discussion's own title
decisions.why: Imported descriptions routinely open on a heading. At its natural size that heading came out larger than the title of the discussion sitting above it, so the page read as though it had two titles and the wrong one won.

decisions.title: The editing box still shows what the author typed, not a rendered version
decisions.why: That text is what gets saved and what an author edits. Hiding it behind a rendered view would mean converting back and forth on every keystroke and risking their wording. The preview answers the same need without touching what is stored.

decisions.title: The stray-mark fix covers discussion descriptions only
decisions.why: The same marks appear on every screen in the app that shows written content. Fixing it everywhere is a change with a wide blast radius and no ticket behind it; fixing it here keeps this job's promise without spending someone else's risk.

decisions.title: The preview is a plain pair of buttons, not a split screen
decisions.why: The description box is three lines tall inside a settings panel. A side-by-side view would have forced the panel wider or the text narrower, for a field most authors fill once.

decisions.title: Existing hand-written descriptions are allowed to reflow
decisions.why: Yours, 2026-08-17: if someone pressed return, students should see the break. Line breaks that were previously thrown away will now show on descriptions nobody imported. Wording and characters are untouched.

decisions.title: No rich editor for a discussion description — the preview is the answer
decisions.why: Yours, 2026-08-17: the description stays as typed text. The author keeps editing the source, and the preview shows them the result. Nothing is raised for a rich editor, and the way a description is stored does not change.

decisions.title: An icon on a heading's line is held to that line, in discussion descriptions only
decisions.why: The import drops the size the course author set, so a small icon arrives at full size and pushes the heading text below it. Rather than guess a size for every image, only images sharing a line with heading text are treated as icons. Banners and dividers, which sit on their own, are untouched.

decisions.title: Two things found inside the import itself were left untouched — they belong to Artur's open work
decisions.why: The import is his, and both sit in changes he has in progress today. Touching them would land my edits in the middle of his, and reporting them as our next steps would put his work on our plan. They are written down below for him instead.

next.if_nothing: The work sits uncommitted in the working copy. Nothing reaches the shared history until you put it there.
